This was a disturbing and deeply embarrassing scene in Gaza City today during the funeral of a man killed in an Israeli airstrike for allegedly being affiliated with Hamas. Members of his clan fired thousands of rounds into the air, initially causing panic and confusion among residents who did not understand what was happening. The spectacle of armed men recklessly discharging weapons sparked widespread anger and contempt among many Gazans, who viewed it as yet another example of the destructive behavior of powerful clans in the Strip.

The incident renewed calls to disarm Gaza's clans and militias and remove weapons from civilian hands to reduce crime, curb intra-Palestinian violence, strengthen the rule of law, and break patterns of behavior that fuel radicalization, intimidation, and the dominance of armed actors over civil society.

Many Palestinians bitterly note the irony that these same clans and armed strongmen, so eager to display their power before fellow Palestinians, tend to disappear when confronted by the Israeli military. Time and again, tribal militias, criminal gangs, and other armed actors avoid direct confrontation with the IDF, yet readily turn their weapons on other Palestinians, whether against Palestinian Authority forces in the past or, at times, even against Hamas itself.

There should be no tolerance for lawlessness. Neither "martyrs" nor their families have the right to terrorize an entire society in the name of archaic notions of honor, death glorification, or tribal privilege. Hamas and Gaza's powerful clans alike must be disarmed, for the sake of Palestinians and Israelis alike.

During the humanitarian mission in Oleshky, Ukrainian military personnel also evacuated 167 civilians from the right bank of Kherson Oblast

During the ceasefire regime introduced in designated areas of Kherson Oblast for the humanitarian mission in Oleshky, the Defense Forces of Ukraine utilized the opportunities created by the security situation to evacuate residents from the right bank of Kherson Oblast.

This refers to settlements in the territory controlled by Ukraine along the Dnipro River, which faced daily shelling by the army of russia. Those who previously had no opportunity to leave the dangerous areas were able to depart.

Specifically, the civil-military cooperation units of the "South" Group of Forces, in cooperation with local authorities, evacuated 167 civilians to safer locations in Kherson Oblast. Among them were 22 children and 21 mobility-impaired individuals who required special attention and assistance.

It is worth noting that the evacuation took place under extremely difficult and dangerous conditions. The routes passed through mined roads that suffered destruction, areas with burned military equipment and civilian cars. All of this significantly complicated movement and required special caution and coordinated actions of all involved units.

Despite these risks, the main priority remains saving the lives of the civilian population and providing assistance to those who cannot independently leave the dangerous territories.

Every saved person is the result of joint work and coordinated interaction of all those involved in the humanitarian mission.

Units of the "South" Group of Forces clearly and strictly adhere to the ceasefire regime in the area of the humanitarian mission.

items.tx:
About Oleshky.

First, thank you to everyone who made this evacuation possible. To everyone who spent years drawing attention to russian genocide in Oleshky, long before the suffering made international headlines. And to everyone who continues fighting to bring home those abducted by russia.

Every single life saved is invaluable.

Watching people finally escape the hell of russian occupation, carrying their pets and a few belongings — whatever was left of their former lives — was both heartbreaking and deeply moving.

russia made these people go through the hell none of us can even imagine. They will need enormous support to rebuild their lives, and I sincerely hope the Ukrainian state will provide it.

And this brings me to the most important point that we should keep conveying to the world.

This evacuation must not become a story about russian goodwill.

None of these people should ever have been forced to live through that hell and flee their homes in the first place.

For years, people in Oleshky have lived under russian occupation, subjected to grave abuses and deprived of their freedom and basic needs. Those atrocities demand thorough investigation and accountability, they must not be written off or forgotten.

Allowing some people to leave does not erase what happened to them. Nor does it absolve russia of responsibility for those who still remain trapped, those who have been abducted, and those who have lost their lives.

As for the russian political motives behind this operation. I fear that Moscow will be trying to present the release of these people as evidence of its supposed willingness to negotiate — and then use that narrative to encourage Washington to double down pressure on Kyiv as if we are an obstacle to peace. 

We are seeing the same story unfolding now, with the lately released American citizen who was illegally abducted by russia and tortured in captivity, but who now plays into Trump's narrative that sanctions againts russia must be lifted.

russia is not humanitarian, it is a perpetrator and a core reason for this war. It is cancer of mankind.

But besides political motives, russians may well try to get military advantages too. While the temporary Oleshky ceasefire made this evacuation possible, we should also be watching further russian military activity in the Kherson direction very closely. There were reports of russia using humanitarian demining to bring in more weapons, improve logistics and do troops rotations.

None of this diminishes the extraordinary importance of the lives saved. Quite the opposite.

But we must keep telling the *full story of Oleshky*. Not just about this evacuation, but the years of occupation, suffering, disappearances, deaths, and the people who are still there, waiting to come home.

Because this mission also reminds us of something fundamental: this war continues only because russia chooses to continue it.

If russia stops fighting, there will be no war. If Ukraine stops fighting, there will be no Ukraine.

"I wanted Ukraine to be back in Oleshky, not people from Oleshky to move here," said a woman with tears in her eyes yesterday. I cannot agree more. This war is so unjust.

Oleshky was, is and will always be Ukraine.
